authorisation: The Product Owner's mission of 2026-11-03 (UX overhaul of Sign-in methods, Client groups, Identity providers and Delivery; investigate the After Check-out emergency fallback warning), under the standing test-appliance deployment authority (D79). The mission did not authorise a merge: the PR waits for the PO's approval.
delivery: Sign-in methods is split into tabs (Methods, By network, Email accounts, One-time codes, Protection), linkable by URL hash; method descriptions are hints, warnings stay visible. Client groups, Identity providers and Delivery dialogs use quiet hints, titled sections and a closed disclosure for advanced fields (scopes, SMTP timeout) and long registration instructions. Email accounts asks for the reason and password only once a value changed. After Check-out Access showed the built-in emergency terms wrongly ('no time', 'Up to 0 devices'): the appliance sends them in the grant's shape (duration_seconds, device_limit_policy, device_limit 0); the console now normalises them (1 hour, no separate device limit, new devices refused). The fallback warning, its critical alerts and the safeguards are unchanged; the warning offers 'Set this site's terms' to roles that can publish.
finding: The fallback warning is correct: the site has no published After Check-out terms (config_version 0, configured false, empty history, policy null, enabled true), so the effective source is EMERGENCY_FALLBACK. Not a persistence or status defect. Nothing was published.
